description: tsapi fixture: a TypeScript Node/Express-style REST API (router with middleware chains, JWT auth, sliding-window rate limiter, Postgres access layer, zod-flavoured request validation, WebSocket notification hub). Tasks describe the developer's intent rather than naming the symbols, so the corpus scores semantic retrieval rather than substring matching.

cases.task: smooth out request throttling so a caller is not handed a full fresh allowance the instant the counting period rolls over
decide who a throttling counter belongs to so a whole office behind one shared address is not punished together
stop the throttling bookkeeping from growing without bound as new callers appear and old ones go away
compare a credential digest against the expected one without letting the time it takes reveal how much of it was right
reject a credential that has aged out, was issued by the wrong party, or was meant for a different service, while tolerating a couple of seconds of clock drift between hosts
make sure the long-lived credential used only for renewal cannot be presented to a normal endpoint as if it were the short-lived one
report every bad field in one round trip instead of stopping at the first problem so a form can highlight all of them at once
turn away a name that is too short and an address that is not shaped like a mailbox before anything reaches storage
let a client walk through a long list page by page without deep pages getting slower and without skipping rows when new ones are inserted mid-scroll
return a friendly conflict message when the short URL name someone picked is already taken, instead of leaking the driver's error code
undo every write in a multi-statement operation when one of the later statements blows up, and always hand the connection back
pull the identifier out of a URL like /projects/abc123 without using a regular expression that could blow up on a hostile input
run the chain of wrappers around a handler in order, letting one of them stop everything after it, and catch the mistake of continuing twice
notice a browser that disappeared without saying goodbye and clean up the connection instead of holding it open forever
stop one signed-in user from listening in on another user's live event stream
refuse an enormous upload while it is still arriving so the process never allocates the whole thing
refuse to start in the live environment when the signing secret is too weak to be safe
after a record is stored, push a live update to whoever is watching that owner's feed
